name: A1-03 HTTP Request - rate limits and back-off

meta.description: How to survive a 429. Spaces requests out with batching, turns the status code into data with Never Error, and tells a retryable error apart from a permanent one. Retry on Fail is deliberately off on the HTTP node here: it only fires when the node throws, and Never Error stops the node throwing.
meta.author: Suyash Raj - https://rajsuyash.com/blog/n8n-error-handling-best-practices.html
meta.setup: None. httpbin.org returns whatever status code you ask it for, so the failure is reproducible on demand.
meta.expectedOutput: 'Call a rate-limited API' runs once per input item with a 1s gap every 5 items. 'Classify the failure' outputs one row per item with retryable: true for 408/425/429/500/502/503/504 and false for 200 and the other 4xx codes, with Retry-After honoured when the server sends it.
meta.failureCases: Change a status code in the 'Synthetic input' Code node to 401 and watch 'Classify the failure' mark it permanent. To see Retry on Fail work, turn Never Error off on 'Call a rate-limited API' and switch Retry on Fail on in Settings: the 429 then fails the node and n8n retries it (2 to 5 tries, at most 5000 ms apart). With Never Error on, a 429 is data, the node never fails, and Retry on Fail does nothing.

nodes.name: Call a rate-limited API
nodes.notes: Three settings do three different jobs. batching spaces requests so you are less likely to be rate-limited at all. Retry on Fail is off here on purpose: n8n retries a node only when it throws, and neverError stops it throwing. neverError + fullResponse put the status code in the output so the next node can decide what it means. Pick one approach per node: let it fail and use Retry on Fail, or let it succeed and branch on the status code.
